to_quote: no Person holding any Office under the United States, shall be a Member of either House during his Continuance in Office

from_quote: the fourth ſection of the ſecond article puts it out of doubt, viz. "The Preſident, Vice Preſident, and all civil officers of the United States, ſhall be removed from office on impeachment, &c."
rationale: The paragraph names "the fourth section of the second article" and quotes it in quotation marks (the printed commas differ slightly from the clause).
to_quote: The President, Vice President and all civil Officers of the United States, shall be removed from Office on Impeachment

from_quote: the Congreſs ſhould have the power of regulating the elections
rationale: The paragraph defends the power of Congress over the regulation of elections, and the exception for the place of electing Senators, which are the content of Article I, Section 4, Clause 1.
to_quote: but the Congress may at any time by Law make or alter such Regulations

from_quote: Why are not the ſalaries of the members of Congreſs aſcertained by the Conſtitution?
rationale: The paragraph answers the objection that the salaries of the members of Congress are not ascertained by the Constitution; the compensation clause of Article I, Section 6, Clause 1 leaves them to be ascertained by law.
to_quote: to be ascertained by Law, and paid out of the Treasury of the United States

from_quote: IT is proper that Congreſs ſhould have the regulation of this matter for another reaſon
rationale: The paragraph gives a further reason why Congress should regulate its members' salaries, the matter left to law in Article I, Section 6, Clause 1.
to_quote: a Compensation for their Services, to be ascertained by Law

from_quote: no member ſhall be eligible to any office which has been created, or whoſe emoluments have been increaſed, ſince the time of his election
rationale: The paragraph restates the first part of Article I, Section 6, Clause 2: no member eligible to an office created, or whose emoluments were increased, during his time.
to_quote: which shall have been created, or the Emoluments whereof shall have been encreased during such time

from_quote: the Senate cannot originate ſuch bills
rationale: The paragraph says the Senate cannot originate money bills but may amend them, which is the content of Article I, Section 7, Clause 1.
to_quote: but the Senate may propose or concur with Amendments as on other Bills

from_quote: the Preſident's diſapprobation, or negative, is nugatory, when two-thirds of each Houſe concur in any meaſure after it has undergone his inſpection
rationale: The paragraph says the president's negative is nugatory when two thirds of each House concur, and speaks of the ten days given him, which describes Article I, Section 7, Clause 2.
to_quote: if approved by two thirds of that House, it shall become a Law

from_quote: all taxes, impoſts, &c. are to be applied only for the common defence and general welfare, of the United States
rationale: The paragraph discusses the purposes for which taxes and imposts are to be applied, the words of Article I, Section 8, Clause 1.
to_quote: to pay the Debts and provide for the common Defence and general Welfare of the United States

from_quote: there are objections made to the grant of the impoſts to Congreſs
rationale: The paragraph answers the objections to the grant of the imposts to Congress, the power given in Article I, Section 8, Clause 1.
to_quote: To lay and collect Taxes, Duties, Imposts and Excises

from_quote: THIS power is lodged with the preſent Congreſs
rationale: The paragraph follows the borrowing clause (Article I, Section 8, Clause 2) and refers to it as "this power".
to_quote: To borrow Money on the credit of the United States

from_quote: THE power of regulating commerce gives great alarm to the enemies of the Conſtitution
rationale: The paragraph discusses "the power of regulating commerce," the power in Article I, Section 8, Clause 3.
to_quote: To regulate Commerce with foreign Nations, and among the several States

from_quote: except what relates to Courts, which will be taken notice of hereafter
rationale: The paragraph says that of these powers, the one that has been objected to is "what relates to Courts," which is the power to constitute inferior tribunals in Article I, Section 8, Clause 9.
to_quote: To constitute Tribunals inferior to the supreme Court

from_quote: BY this regulation every Houſe of Repreſentatives will have a ſhare in the appropriations; and no miſchief can enſue from appropriations of two years
rationale: The paragraph defends the limit of two years on appropriations for the army, which is in Article I, Section 8, Clause 12.
to_quote: no Appropriation of Money to that Use shall be for a longer Term than two Years

from_quote: BY theſe clauſes, the appointment of the militia officers, and training the militia, are reſerved to the reſpective States
rationale: The paragraph says the appointment of the militia officers and the training of the militia are reserved to the states, which is the reservation in Article I, Section 8, Clause 16.
to_quote: reserving to the States respectively, the Appointment of the Officers, and the Authority of training the Militia

from_quote: THESE clauſes have been extremely miſunderſtood
rationale: The paragraph takes up objections to the congressional command of the militia in "these clauses," the two militia clauses printed above (Article I, Section 8, Clauses 15 and 16).
to_quote: To provide for calling forth the Militia to execute the Laws of the Union

from_quote: the abſolute unqualified command that Congreſs have over the militia
rationale: The paragraph takes up the objection that Congress has an "absolute unqualified command" over the militia, which refers to the militia clauses of Article I, Section 8, Clause 16 (and 15).
to_quote: To provide for organizing, arming, and disciplining, the Militia

from_quote: So great is the jealouſy of ſome of our citizens, that even this clauſe has excited their fears. This little ſpot is to be the centre
rationale: The paragraph answers the fears excited by "this clause" about the seat of government, the district clause printed above it (Article I, Section 8, Clause 17).
to_quote: exclusive Legislation in all Cases whatsoever

from_quote: THE Congreſs is to govern, as they ſhall ſee fit, a diſtrict not more than ten miles ſquare
rationale: The paragraph says Congress is to govern a district not more than ten miles square, as Article I, Section 8, Clause 17 provides.
to_quote: over such District (not exceeding ten Miles square)

from_quote: BY this clauſe, Congreſs have no farther legiſlative authority than ſhall be deemed neceſſary to carry into execution the powers veſted by this Conſtitution
rationale: The paragraph says that by "this clause" Congress has no further authority than is necessary to carry into execution the powers vested by the Constitution, which is the last clause of Article I, Section 8.
to_quote: for carrying into Execution the foregoing Powers, and all other Powers vested by this Constitution

from_quote: THIS clauſe is a proof of deference in the members of the Convention, to each other, and of conceſſion of the northern to the ſouthern States
rationale: The paragraph discusses "this clause" as a concession to the southern states and says the members from South-Carolina and Georgia insisted on it, referring to the clause on migration and importation (Article I, Section 9, Clause 1) printed above it.
to_quote: The Migration or Importation of such Persons as any of the States now existing shall think proper to admit

from_quote: BY this clauſe the Congreſs have the right of ſuſpending the habeas corpus
rationale: The paragraph explains the right of suspending the habeas corpus, which is the subject of Article I, Section 9, Clause 2.
to_quote: The Privilege of the Writ of Habeas Corpus shall not be suspended

from_quote: ex poſt facto laws were dangerous in their principle, and oppreſſive in their execution
rationale: The paragraph defends the ban on ex post facto laws and bills of attainder against an objection "made a part of this clause," the clause printed above it (Article I, Section 9, Clause 3).
to_quote: No Bill of Attainder or ex post facto Law shall be passed

from_quote: THIS clauſe is a confirmation of the third clauſe of the ſecond ſection of the firſt article
rationale: The paragraph names "the third clause of the second section of the first article," which is Article I, Section 2, Clause 3.
to_quote: Representatives and direct Taxes shall be apportioned among the several States

from_quote: THIS clauſe is a confirmation of
rationale: The paragraph refers to "this clause," the clause on capitation and direct taxes printed above it (Article I, Section 9, Clause 4), as confirming Article I, Section 2, Clause 3.
to_quote: No Capitation, or other direct, Tax shall be laid, unless in Proportion to the Census or enumeration

from_quote: ALL writers upon finance hold taxes upon exports to be impolitic
rationale: The paragraph discusses taxes upon exports and says it would be unjust for some states' produce to be taxed for the benefit of others, which concerns the ban on export taxes in Article I, Section 9, Clause 5.
to_quote: No Tax or Duty shall be laid on Articles exported from any State

from_quote: The latter part of the clauſe provides that all Naval Officers fees and port charges ſhall be the ſame throughout the United States; and that a veſſel bound to one State from another, and calling at any intermediate State, ſhall not be obliged to enter, clear, or pay duty, in ſuch State
rationale: The paragraph explains the latter part of the clause, on vessels bound to or from a state not being obliged to enter, clear or pay duties in another, which is Article I, Section 9, Clause 6.
to_quote: nor shall Vessels bound to, or from, one State, be obliged to enter, clear, or pay Duties in another

from_quote: AS all appropriations of money are to be made by law, and regular ſtatements thereof publiſhed
rationale: The paragraph restates the requirement that appropriations be made by law and statements of public money be published, which is Article I, Section 9, Clause 7.
to_quote: No Money shall be drawn from the Treasury, but in Consequence of Appropriations made by Law

from_quote: THE firſt part of this clauſe proves the Convention had no ariſtocratical views
rationale: The paragraph discusses the two parts of "this clause," the clause on titles of nobility and foreign emoluments printed above it (Article I, Section 9, Clause 8).
to_quote: No Title of Nobility shall be granted by the United States

from_quote: THE States, in their individual capacities, ſhould be reſtrained from the exerciſe of the powers enumerated in this clauſe
rationale: The paragraph gives reasons for each of the restraints on the states in "this clause" (treaties, letters of marque, coinage, bills of credit, tender, impairing contracts), the clause printed above it (Article I, Section 10, Clause 1).
to_quote: No State shall enter into any Treaty, Alliance, or Confederation

from_quote: it was highly reaſonable that one State ſhould be prohibited from laying an export duty on the articles of a ſiſter State
rationale: The paragraph defends the bar on state duties on imports and exports, which is Article I, Section 10, Clause 2.
to_quote: No State shall, without the Consent of the Congress, lay any Imposts or Duties on Imports or Exports

from_quote: By this clauſe, a door is open to the States, to raiſe their reſpective quotas, in lieu of direct taxes; by laying a duty upon exports; or even duties upon imports
rationale: The paragraph discusses the state duties on imports and exports allowed by "this clause" and Congress's power of revision, which is Article I, Section 10, Clause 2.
to_quote: the net Produce of all Duties and Imposts, laid by any State on Imports or Exports, shall be for the Use of the Treasury of the United States

from_quote: See in particular the addreſs and reaſons, &c. of the Pennſylvania Minority
rationale: The note refers the reader to "the address and reasons, &c. of the Pennsylvania Minority," which is the Dissent of the Minority of the Convention of Pennsylvania (December 18, 1787), before this pamphlet (1788).

from_quote: Minority addreſs, p. 22 23
rationale: The note cites "Minority address," with pages, the Dissent of the Minority of the Convention of Pennsylvania (December 18, 1787); the link goes to the work as a whole.

from_quote: Minority addreſs. That haſty and paſſionate performance is full of abſurdities upon this head.
rationale: The note names the "Minority address," the Dissent of the Minority of the Convention of Pennsylvania (December 18, 1787), and says it is full of absurdities on this head.

from_quote: I CONCEIVE that the Senators are not impeachable, an• therefore Governor Randolph's objection falls to the ground
rationale: The paragraph says Senators are not impeachable and that "Governor Randolph's objection falls to the ground"; Randolph's letter (October 10, 1787) asks, in its fifty-third paragraph, for a tribunal other than the Senate for the impeachment of Senators.
to_quote: in providing a tribunal inſtead of the Senate for the impeachment of Senators
